text:
jia: quick heads-up while bringing up orion-lite-v3 (int4) on staging — mixed zh+ar prompts sometimes get stray RTL marks and punctuation reordering in the generated text. repro steps below.

jia: repro (simple):
```bash
# request via internal test runner
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TEST_KEY' \
  -d '{"model":"orion-lite-v3","quantize":"int4","input":"简体: 你好。\nعربي: السلام عليكم." }'
```

jia: sample bad output (copied raw, note the \u200F RLM chars and punctuation shift):
```
简体: 你好。.\u200Fعربي: السلام عليكم\u200F.
```

jia: expected:
```
简体: 你好。
عربي: السلام عليكم.
```

samir: can you attach the exact token ids / tokenizer.decode for that input on int4 vs fp16? sounds like tokenization or detokenization is diverging after quantization.

jia: attaching quick diff I ran locally — fp16 decode preserves order, int4 decode inserts U+200F around the Arabic segment. I can paste token lists if helpful.

anya: small eval on our mixed-script subset (1.2k sentences) — BLEU: fp16=32.1 -> int4=29.4 (drop 2.7), chrF: 54.8 -> 52.2. Failure mode frequency ~3.8% (RLM in middle or punctuation mis-attach).

eval-bot: :warning: Regression alert for model onboarding: orion-lite-v3 int4 on "mixedscript-multilang-v1" dataset: BLEU drop 2.7 (p<0.01). See dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/evals/alerts/3555554321

kevin: short term: we can postprocess to strip U+200F / U+202A..U+202E range for mixed requests as a mitigation. longer term we should figure out why detok differs. possibilities: token-to-string mapping table changed after quantized kernel reorder, or SMT detokenizer relies on float rounding in logits that changes tokenization boundary.

samir: plan: 1) run tokenizer-only roundtrip (encode->decode) with the quantized detokenizer code path; 2) compare token ids for boundary tokens between fp16 and int4; 3) run model-only decode with logits forced to fp16 but detok using int4 codepath to isolate stage. I'll bisect the runtime kernels if tokenizer-only passes.

anya: I'll add a unit test to our eval harness for this exact snippet + a small mixedscript fixture so we don't regress silently.

deploy-bot: Created canary rollout: orion-lite-v3-int4 -> canary-tag c-rlm-fix with fallback to orion-lite-v3-fp16 on mixedscript route (threshold 2% errors).

kevin: also flag to infra: ensure we log token id sequence and detokenized string for any request that triggers a RLM insertion so we can triage.

jia: thanks. samir can you own the bisect? I can pick up the eval harness test and the small postprocess shim for the API layer.

samir: yep, I’ll start a bisect now and post findings here.

anya: fwiw, this looks different from prior CJK-only issues — those were subtoken merges. here it's an insertion of control chars around an adjacent RTL segment. probably a detok edge case.

jia: yep — raising so product teams routing mixed-locale UIs are aware. will update the onboarding checklist to include mixedscript smoke. :memo:

samir: preliminary bisect shows suspect 2 commits earlier in the quantized detokenizer refactor — reproducer attached in the branch mr/rlm-detok-bisect.

jia: awesome. leave a note if you need a model snapshot for debugging.

kevin: long-term, consider adding mixed-script tokenization fuzzing into our quantization QA matrix.

deploy-bot: Canary rollback will trigger automatically if error rate > 2.5% for 10m.

anya: assigning follow-ups: samir (bisect + PR), jia (api shim + checklist), anya (eval test + results dashboard).

jia: thanks all. will post updates here as we get fixes. :white_check_mark:
